standard.title: Technical Guidelines for Paint Spray Booths

notes: THIS DOCUMENT HAS NO PEOPLE-COMPETENCY CONTENT AT ALL, and that is the finding that matters for Phase 5. All 9 pages were rendered and read. GU42 does not name a single competent person, trained person, certified operator or examiner. There is no training requirement, no certification, no licence, no validity period, no competent-person examination of the local exhaust ventilation and no examination interval of any kind. The scoping document's Phase 5 table groups GU42 with GU50 and GU43 under people and competency; on the evidence of the document that grouping is wrong for GU42. It belongs with the quantitative engineering modules, and 'competencies' below is deliberately empty rather than padded. THE EXPECTATION THAT IT CARRIES EXPOSURE LIMITS IS ALSO WRONG, though less so than for GU43: GU42 carries no occupational exposure limits — no ppm, no mg/m3, no TLV for any paint or solvent — but it DOES carry a substantial set of numeric ENGINEERING limits (face velocity, water circulation rate, stack height, exhaust velocity, separation distances, overspray control by application rate). Those are all recorded in limits below and they are what makes the module verdict-bearing. The catalogue's evidence_type for GU42 is 'unknown' with a note guessing 'likely LEV thorough examination'. THAT GUESS IS WRONG and should be corrected: there is no thorough examination requirement in this document. The correct evidence_type is a measured engineering inspection of the booth — air velocity, water circulation, stack, separations — which is closest to 'checklist' plus instrument readings, not a third-party certificate. WHY module_kind = compliance: a competent inspector with an anemometer, a tape measure and the booth's paint consumption figure can produce a genuine COMPLIANT / NON-COMPLIANT verdict against stated DM numbers, with no external standard needed. Version 'V 4.0' and issue date 09/05/2024 come from the page footers of the document itself, not the filename and not the portal record date of 2024-07-25. THE DATE IS AMBIGUOUS AS PRINTED BUT HAS SINCE BEEN RESOLVED, and the resolved reading is used here. The cover and footers print '09/05/2024' numerically with both components <= 12, and the superseded date beside it, 04/10/2021, is ALSO ambiguous on the same test, so the page gives no corroboration either way — unlike GU66 and GU99, where the superseded date carries a day above 12 and settles the order from the print alone. catalogue_editions_resolved.json settles GU42 as day_first at HIGH confidence using evidence outside the page: the PDF's embedded timestamps, /CreationDate (D:20240709123727+04'00') and xmp:CreateDate 2024-07-09T12:37:27+04:00, put the export at 9 July 2024, making the month-first reading (5 September 2024) a future date at export and therefore impossible. GU38, GU42 and GU43 were all exported in that same 9 July 2024 session and resolve by the same argument. Both candidate readings fall in 2024, so there is no year risk. Recorded as 2024-05-09 with high confidence on that basis. TWO DELEGATIONS: respiratory protection is delegated to 'the Health and Safety Department Technical Guideline regarding Respiratory Protection' (p9), which is not named by number; and the powder-coating ventilation duty is expressed against the lower explosive limit 'for the materials being applied', a value the document does not supply for any material. Neither can be resolved from GU42 alone.

limits.parameter_label: Air velocity over the open face of a dry-type spray booth
limits.display: not less than 30 to 75 linear m/min
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to dry type spray booths, over-spray dry filters and filter rolls, maintained to collect the overspray during spraying operations.
limits.source_quote: The air velocity of not less than 30 to 75 linear m/min over the open face of the booth shall be maintained to collect the overspray in spraying operations.
limits.note: AMBIGUOUS AS PRINTED AND ONLY PARTLY ENCODED, per the section 7.12 'omit an ambiguous cell, never guess it' rule. 'Not less than 30 to 75' is self-contradictory: a minimum cannot be a range. Page 6 was rendered and read to rule out a transcription artefact — the printed line really does read that way. Only the unambiguous half is encoded: 30 linear m/min is a floor, inclusive by the 'not less than' glyph, and a booth measuring below 30 is non-compliant on any reading. The 75 is deliberately NOT encoded as max_val, because it is not determinable from the document whether it is the top of a recommended band, a design target for larger booths, or a ceiling. Encoding it as a ceiling would fail a booth running at 80 m/min on a number the document may never have intended as a limit. Only DM can resolve it. Contrast the water-curtain clause at 4-2-5, which states a clean single-sided minimum of 30 m/min with no second figure.

limits.parameter_label: Average draft velocity over the open face of a water curtain / water wash spray booth
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to a water curtain booth or a water wash spray booth fitted with a water curtain. Stated as an AVERAGE over the open face, so a single spot reading is not sufficient evidence — the measurement method must traverse the face.
limits.source_quote: The average draft velocity over the open face of the booth shall be not less than 30 m/min.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum by the 'not less than' glyph. Unambiguous, unlike the dry-filter figure above.

limits.parameter_label: Water circulation rate of a water curtain booth, per unit of exhaust air
limits.unit: litres per 1000 m3 of exhaust air
limits.display: not less than 150 liters/1000 m3 of exhaust air
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to water curtain and water wash spray booths. A ratio, not an absolute flow: the required litres depend on the booth's exhaust air volume, so the exhaust volume must be known before this can be judged.
limits.source_quote: Water circulation rate shall be not less than 150 liters/1000 m3 of exhaust air.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. The document does not state whether the exhaust air figure is per minute or per hour, so the ratio is dimensionally incomplete as printed; in practice it is read as litres per minute per 1000 m3 per minute of exhaust, but that is inference and is NOT encoded. Flagged rather than assumed.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum exhaust stack height above the maximum roof level of the process building
limits.display: minimum height of 1.5 meters or higher in sensitive locations above the maximum roof level of the process building
limits.qualifier_rule: Measured above the MAXIMUM roof level of the process building, not above the stack base. A vertical stack is required. 'Or higher in sensitive locations, as per standard' — neither 'sensitive location' nor the standard referred to is defined in this document, so the 1.5 m figure is a floor that may be raised by a requirement GU42 does not contain.
limits.source_quote: The gaseous laden air shall be exhausted through a vertical stack having a minimum height of 1.5 meters or higher in sensitive locations above the maximum roof level of the process building, as per standard.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum ('minimum height of'). The escalation for sensitive locations is real but unquantified and must not be auto-applied.

limits.parameter_label: Exhaust gas velocity at the stack
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to the exhaust stack discharging gaseous laden air from the spray booth.
limits.source_quote: The exhaust gas velocity should not be less than 8m/sec.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum by the 'not less than' glyph. Note the verb is 'should', not 'shall', unlike the stack height in the clause immediately above it — the document mixes mandatory and advisory language within a single sub-section, which matters if a non-compliance is ever contested.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum separation between a spray booth and other operations
limits.display: not less than 3 meters, or a greater distance and partition or wall
limits.qualifier_rule: Each spray booth shall be separated from other operations by at least this distance, OR by a greater distance together with a partition or wall such as to reduce the danger from hazardous operations. The alternative is not a substitute for the distance but an escalation of it.
limits.source_quote: Each spray booth shall be separated from other operations by not less than 3 meters or by a greater distance and partition or wall as to reduce the danger from hazardous operations.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Distinct from the 6 m ignition-source exclusion below — different distance, different hazard, and a site can satisfy one while failing the other.

limits.parameter_label: Exclusion distance for open flame or spark producing equipment from a spraying area
limits.display: no open flame or spark producing equipment or operation within 6 meters unless separated by a non-combustible partition
limits.qualifier_rule: The distance may be dispensed with entirely where a non-combustible partition separates the ignition source from the spraying area — the document offers the partition as a full alternative here, unlike the 3 m separation clause where the partition accompanies a greater distance.
limits.source_quote: There shall be no open flame or spark producing equipment or operation in any spraying area within 6 meters unless separated by a non-combustible partition.
limits.note: Inclusivity at exactly 6 m is genuinely ambiguous and is recorded as inclusive only because the prohibition reads 'within 6 meters', which conventionally includes the boundary; the document uses no <, >, <= or >= glyph here. Flagged per rule 6. A source sitting at exactly 6.0 m should be treated as a query, not as an automatic failure.

limits.parameter_label: Recommended overspray control — application rate below 2 litres/hour
limits.display: Less than 2 liters/hour: Water curtain, fibers, baffles
limits.qualifier_rule: Selection rule, not a performance limit: at this application rate any of a water curtain, fibre filters or baffles is an acceptable overspray control. Baffle plates are acceptable only for small paint rates or where paint is applied electrostatically.
limits.source_quote: Application rate: Less than 2 liters/hour | Recommended overspray control: Water curtain, fibers, baffles
limits.note: Exclusive upper bound by the 'Less than' glyph, per rule 6. Page 6 was rendered and read to confirm the two-column mapping by position: left column is the application rate, right column the recommended control. The three bands abut with no gap and no overlap — below 2, 2 to 4 inclusive, above 4 — so unlike the band tables warned about in section 7.12 there is no NOT_ASSESSED hole. The column header says 'Recommended', which weakens this from a requirement to guidance.

limits.parameter_label: Recommended overspray control — application rate 2 to 4 litres/hour
limits.qualifier_rule: Selection rule: at this application rate a water curtain or fibre filters are acceptable. Baffles drop out of the acceptable list at this band.
limits.source_quote: Application rate: 2 to 4 liters/hour | Recommended overspray control: Water curtain, fiber
limits.note: Both bounds inclusive: the adjacent bands are 'Less than 2' and 'More than 4', which leaves exactly 2 and exactly 4 to this band by elimination. This is one of the rare cases where band inclusivity is determinable from the table's own construction rather than from a glyph.

limits.parameter_label: Recommended overspray control — application rate above 4 litres/hour
limits.qualifier_rule: Selection rule: above 4 litres/hour only a water curtain is an acceptable overspray control. Fibre filters and baffles are both excluded.
limits.source_quote: Application rate: More than 4 liters/hour | Recommended overspray control: Water Curtain
limits.note: Exclusive lower bound by the 'More than' glyph, per rule 6.

limits.parameter_label: Powder coating booth atmosphere relative to the lower explosive limit
limits.display: exhaust ventilation shall be enough to maintain the atmosphere below the lower explosive limit for the materials being applied
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to powder coating operations. The threshold is the LEL of the specific material being applied.
limits.source_quote: The exhaust ventilation shall be enough to maintain the atmosphere below the lower explosive limit for the materials being applied.
limits.note: DELIBERATELY LEFT UNQUANTIFIED — min_val and max_val are null because the document supplies no number. The limit is the LEL of whichever powder is in use, and GU42 lists no LELs and names no source for them; nor does it apply the customary safety fraction (many regimes require 10 or 25 percent of LEL rather than 100 percent). Encoding a percentage here would be inventing a limit. Recorded so the obligation is visible, with the value left for the material's own safety data. The 'below' glyph is exclusive, which is the one thing that is determinable.

obligations.cadence_note: After each period of use — an activity-driven cadence, not a calendar one, so no cadence_months or cadence_days can be set. Clogged filter pads or rolls shall be discarded and replaced; discarded pads must go into a closed metal container and be set aside immediately to a safe, well-detached location. A dial gauge or manometer should be fitted to indicate static pressure drop across the filters, which is the practical trigger for replacement.
obligations.trigger_event: after each period of use of a dry-type booth
obligations.applies_to: Filter pads and filter rolls in dry type spray booths and over-spray dry filters
obligations.source_quote: Filter pads/rolls should be inspected after each period of use and clogged filter pads/rolls shall be discarded and replaced. All discarded filter pads/rolls shall be placed in a closed metal container and immediately set aside to a safe well-detached location. A dial gauge or manometer should be fitted to indicate static pressure drop across the filters. (p7)

obligations.cadence_note: NO INTERVAL IS SET BY DM. The document delegates the maintenance cadence to the equipment manufacturer: procedures 'should be established or follow the manufacturer's recommendation'. This is an honest null of the delegating kind — the duty exists, the frequency comes from the booth's own manual and will differ site to site. It also means the app cannot compute a due date for booth maintenance from guideline content; it must take the interval from the client's equipment documentation.
obligations.trigger_event: before excessive restriction to air flow occurs
obligations.source_quote: Maintenance procedures should be established or follow the manufacturer's recommendation on operation to ensure replacing filter pads before excessive restriction to air flow occurs. (p6)

obligations.cadence_note: Continuous standing duty with no interval — spraying areas are to be kept as free from accumulated combustible residue deposits 'as practicable, by cleaning'. Residue scrapings and contaminated debris must be removed from the premises IMMEDIATELY and properly disposed of, which is an event-driven promptness requirement rather than a cadence. Cleaning tools (scrapers, spuds) must be of non-sparking material. Exhaust ducts are to be fitted with several access doors when necessary to facilitate cleaning, and baffle plates must be readily removable or accessible on both sides for cleaning.
obligations.applies_to: All spraying areas, spray booth interiors, baffle plates and exhaust ducts
obligations.source_quote: All spraying areas shall be kept as free from the accumulation of deposits of combustible residues as practicable, by cleaning. Scrapers, spuds, or other such tools used for cleaning purposes shall be of non-sparking material. Residue scrapings and debris contaminated with residue shall be immediately removed from the premises and properly disposed of. (p8)

obligations.cadence_note: 'The container should be emptied regularly' — 'regularly' is not quantified anywhere in the document. Honest null. Metal waste cans must be provided wherever rags and waste are impregnated with finishing materials, and contaminated rags or combustible material must be disposed of in a metal container with a metal lid.
obligations.applies_to: Metal containers holding rags or other combustible material contaminated with paint or solvent
obligations.source_quote: Any rags or other combustible material contaminated with paint/solvent should be disposed of in a metal container with metal lid. The container should be emptied regularly. (p5) Metal waste cans shall be provided wherever rags and waste are impregnated with finishing materials. (p8)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing operational requirement, no cadence. Mechanical ventilation adequate to remove flammable vapour, mist or powders shall ALWAYS be kept in operation while spraying is conducted AND for a sufficient time thereafter — 'sufficient time' is not quantified, so the purge period cannot be checked against a number. Each booth shall have an independent exhaust duct discharging to the exterior, except that multiple booths using identical spray material may share a common exhaust. Exhausted air shall not be recirculated.
obligations.trigger_event: during spraying operations and for a sufficient time afterwards
obligations.applies_to: Mechanical ventilation and exhaust duct systems serving all spraying areas
obligations.source_quote: All spraying areas shall be provided with mechanical ventilation adequate to remove flammable vapor, mist, or powders. Mechanical ventilation shall always be kept in operation while spray operations are being conducted and for a sufficient time thereafter. Each spray booth shall have an independent exhaust duct system discharging to the exterior of the building except that multiple spray booths in which identical spray material is used, may have a common exhaust. Air exhausted from spray operations shall not be recirculated. (p8)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing electrical and ignition-control requirement, no cadence and — worth noting for a client with an electrical inspection regime — NO earth continuity test interval. All metal parts of spray booths, exhaust ducts and piping systems conveying flammable or combustible liquid shall be properly electrically grounded. No portable electrical lamps during spraying; if used for cleaning or repair they must be of a type approved for hazardous locations. Illumination of spraying areas shall be through glass panels or other transparent materials, with precautions against accumulated residue on exposed panels being heated by the light source.
obligations.applies_to: Spray booth metalwork, exhaust ducts, flammable liquid piping, and spraying area illumination
obligations.source_quote: All metal parts of spray booths, exhaust ducts and piping systems conveying flammable or combustible liquid shall be properly electrically grounded. (p8) No portable electrical lamps shall be used in any spraying area during spraying operations. If used during cleaning or repair operations, they shall be of the type approved for hazardous locations. (p8) Illumination of spraying areas shall be through glass panels or other transparent materials. (p7)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing requirement. 'An adequate number' of suitable portable fire extinguishers shall be installed near the spraying area — the number is not specified and no inspection or servicing interval for the extinguishers is given here. Firefighting equipment should be readily available in hand during mixing, decanting and transferring. Honest null on both count and cadence.
obligations.applies_to: Portable fire extinguishers near the spraying area, and firefighting equipment at paint and solvent mixing, decanting and transfer operations
obligations.source_quote: An adequate number of suitable portable fire extinguishers shall be installed near the spraying area. (p8) Firefighting equipment should be readily available in hand. (p5)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing requirement, no cadence. Closest available vocabulary term; the duty is signage. 'No Smoking' signs shall be posted at all spraying areas and paint storage rooms, and naked flames and lighted cigarettes are not permitted where operations produce flammable vapours. Noted per rule 4 — the closed vocabulary has no signage type.
obligations.applies_to: All spraying areas and paint storage rooms
obligations.source_quote: 'No Smoking' signs shall be posted at all spraying areas and paint storage rooms. (p9) Naked flames and lighted cigarettes shall not be permitted. (p5)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing PPE requirement with no inspection, replacement or fit-testing cadence. Chemical cartridge respirators or masks shall be provided and used IN ADDITION to engineering controls — the document is explicit that PPE supplements rather than replaces the ventilation. Where ventilation is restricted, as in confined spaces, respiratory protection and breathing apparatus shall be provided. The detail is delegated to a separate Health and Safety Department Technical Guideline on Respiratory Protection which GU42 does not identify by number.
obligations.trigger_event: spraying operations; work in confined spaces where ventilation is restricted
obligations.applies_to: Spray booth operators — chemical cartridge respirators or masks; breathing apparatus in confined spaces
obligations.source_quote: In addition to the engineering controls to ensure that the atmosphere is free from suspended paint spray or powder, chemical cartridge respirators or masks shall be provided and used. Reference should be made to the Health and Safety Department Technical Guideline regarding Respiratory Protection. (p9) When working in confined spaces, where ventilation is restricted, respiratory protection and the provision of breathing apparatus shall be provided. (p5)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing welfare requirement rather than a periodic task. Adequate washing facilities including hand cleansers shall be made available, and workers shall be INSTRUCTED to use them before any lunch break and after work — a per-shift behavioural duty, not a maintainable cadence. Note the express prohibition on cleaning hands or any part of the body with solvents; solvent use is restricted to cleaning spray nozzles and auxiliary equipment.
obligations.trigger_event: before any lunch break and after work
obligations.applies_to: Spray booth workers — washing facilities and hand cleansers
obligations.source_quote: Adequate washing facilities, including hand cleansers, shall be made available. Workers shall be instructed to use such facilities before any lunch break and after work. (p5) The sure of solvents for cleaning operations shall be restricted to clean spray nozzles and auxiliary equipment. Employees should not clean their hands or other parts of the body with solvents. (p8)

obligations.cadence_note: Event-driven, no cadence. All paint or solvent spillage should be mopped up without delay. Special precautions shall be followed when working with paint that may contain lead, to prevent absorption through skin, swallowing or inhalation of fumes — but the precautions themselves are NOT specified anywhere in the document, and no lead exposure limit, air monitoring requirement or blood-lead screening is set. That is a material gap for any client spraying lead-containing paint.
obligations.trigger_event: paint or solvent spillage; use of paint which may contain lead
obligations.applies_to: Spillage during mixing, decanting and transferring; and work with lead-containing paint
obligations.source_quote: All paint/solvent spillage should be mopped up without delay. (p5) When working with paint which may contain lead, special precautions shall be followed to prevent absorption through skin, swallowing or inhalation of the fumes. (p5)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing prohibition, no cadence. Spraying shall not be conducted outside predetermined spraying areas — a containment rule that is checkable on inspection.
obligations.applies_to: All spraying operations at the establishment
obligations.source_quote: Spraying shall not be conducted outside of predetermined spraying areas. (p8)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing requirement specific to powder coating. All non-deposited air-suspended powders shall be safely removed via exhaust ducts to the powder recovery cyclone in series with fabric filters. No cadence, and no cleaning or filter-change interval for the cyclone or the fabric filters.
obligations.applies_to: Powder coating operations — powder recovery cyclone in series with fabric filters
obligations.source_quote: All non-deposited air-suspended powders shall be safely removed via exhaust ducts to the powder recovery cyclone in series with fabric filters. (p9)
